issues.claim: Онлайн-операции поддерживаются не во всех редакциях SQL Server: это возможность редакции Enterprise, а также Azure SQL Database и Azure SQL Managed Instance.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt only says online operations are not available in every edition and points to the 'Editions and supported features of SQL Server 2025' table. It does not show that Enterprise is the only on-premises edition. Developer and Evaluation editions also support it. I cannot confirm from the excerpts whether SQL Server 2025 changed Standard edition availability. The generator flagged the same open point.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to be version-neutral: 'Online operations are available in Enterprise-level editions of SQL Server (Enterprise, Developer, Evaluation) and in Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance; check the edition feature table for your SQL Server version.' Apply the same change to the ru and en text.

issues.claim: нагрузку на `tempdb` (сортировка, хранилище версий при онлайн-построении)
issues.problem: By default the index sort runs in the user database. It runs in tempdb only when SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON. Listing sorting as a tempdb load without that qualifier is imprecise. The version store point is correct, although it moves to the persistent version store when Accelerated Database Recovery is enabled.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'the load on tempdb (the version store during an online build, and sorting if SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON)'. Apply the same change to the ru and en text.

issues.claim: Какие блокировки держит построение индекса и как долго, где хранятся промежуточные данные и что будет, если операцию придётся прервать на середине?
issues.problem: The hint maps almost one-to-one onto the correct options (online, tempdb/log space, resumable). It is a little too revealing for a multi question, though it does not name any option.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten to a nudge, for example: 'What does the build hold on the table and for how long, and what happens if you have to stop it halfway?'. Mirror the change in en.

issues.claim: Для SQL Server JSON-столбец - это текст: у путей внутри него нет типов, ограничений и статистики
issues.problem: The fetched 'Index JSON data' excerpt states that the native json data type and JSON indexes are generally available in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance. It also says the JSON index is the recommended approach for the json type. The text states 'JSON is text' as a universal fact and never names a version. A lead in 2026 would learn an outdated picture. The promotion path (computed column plus index) is still correct for nvarchar storage and for indexing a single strongly typed property.
issues.suggestedFix: Qualify by version. Say that in SQL Server 2022 and earlier, and when JSON is stored in nvarchar, it is plain text indexed only through computed columns. Add that SQL Server 2025 and Azure SQL have the native json type and CREATE JSON INDEX, which can replace per-property computed columns for many predicates. Mention in answer item 4 or 5 that CHECK (ISJSON) is unnecessary for the json type. Consider setting meta.dotnetVersion or stating the assumed SQL Server version in the prompt.

issues.claim: токен параллелизма (`rowversion`) или точечное изменение через `JSON_MODIFY`
issues.problem: JSON_MODIFY in a single UPDATE protects only against concurrent changes to different paths. Two writers changing the same path still get last-writer-wins. It is not a general lost-update protection like a rowversion token. Presenting the two as equal alternatives is imprecise.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'a concurrency token (rowversion) is the reliable option; a targeted UPDATE ... JSON_MODIFY on a single path avoids overwriting other paths but does not detect conflicting changes to the same path.' Apply the same change to the ru and en text.

issues.claim: Запрос с этим выражением получает поиск по индексу и статистику
issues.problem: The computed column is defined as CAST(JSON_VALUE(...) AS nvarchar(50)). A query that uses plain JSON_VALUE(Attributes,'$.color') without the same CAST may not match the computed column expression, and the index may not be used.
issues.suggestedFix: Add: 'queries should filter on the computed column Color (or repeat the exact same expression, including the CAST)'. Apply the same change to the ru and en text.
